name: CityScapes
line: Two to four hours inside the city, at the six places it would rather you did not look at.
deck: The eco-walks, renamed. A river bank, a landfill, a ridge forest, a heritage water system — all of it already inside Delhi, all of it reachable before lunch.

aims.p: The objective is a trip that needs no night away and no budget line. If it takes a fortnight to arrange, it does not happen.

aims.h: Stop at what people drive past
aims.p: The aim is not to show anybody somewhere new. It is to make somebody stand still at a place they already pass twice a week.
This is meant to be the trip a school takes before it risks a longer one, and to cost little enough that risking it is easy.

aims.h: Give the same group a second reason
aims.p: Six of them exist so a class can come back to a different argument in the same city instead of ticking the city off.

how.h: Two to four hours, and no coach
how.p: Short enough for a school morning or a Saturday. A river, a forest and a landfill are each under an hour away.
Yamuna, landfill, forest, bird watching, heritage, restoration park. Every one of them is somewhere Delhi already is. The walk is only the part where somebody points.
No overnight, no permission slip for a night away, no coach across three states. It is also how a school finds out whether its students want the twelve-day version.

route.note: The river, at the point where the city meets it.
A hill made entirely of what Delhi threw out.
The Ridge — dry, thorny, and older than the city on top of it.
Water-harvesting works built by people who had no pumps.
A park in the middle of being put back.

who.h: Delhi schools with one free morning
who.p: The unit is a class and a Saturday, or a class and a games period.

who.h: People who have driven past all six places
who.p: Everybody in this city has passed the river, the ridge and the landfill. This is for the ones who have never stopped at any of them.

who.h: Groups that are not ready for a journey
who.p: Some cohorts should not be put on a bus for twelve days first. An afternoon is a cheaper way to find that out than day three of twelve.

done.p: More than a thousand walks in two decades, and over a hundred thousand people on them. It was built two dozen people at a time.

holes.what: Thirteen frames catalogued here as photographs of these walks have been withdrawn: they are not photographs and were never ours. What is left is a real archive in which which of the six walks each frame was taken on is still recorded nowhere, and two of the six have no frame at all.
holes.unlocks: A walk name against each frame, and any photograph at all of the heritage walk or the restoration park. It would let the six walks above carry a photograph each instead of a line each.

holes.what: A thousand walks and a hundred thousand people, and we cannot tell you which of the six walks people ask for.
holes.unlocks: Any per-walk count would let this page rank its own routes instead of listing them.

statement.line: Distance was never the reason nobody went.
statement.under: Every one of the six is inside the city limits. Whatever has kept people away, it was not the map.
